title: Bhishma Parva (the Gita re-read in place, 6 sessions)
hook: between two armies, a warrior asks his charioteer to be his teacher, and the charioteer smiles.
carry: I am your disciple, teach me

segments.voice: Yesterday the conches roared, and Arjuna sat down in his chariot with his bow at his feet. Your line: a man sitting still.

A chariot stands alone in the open ground, with an army on either side, waiting. The warrior in it is a great archer, and he has just put his bow down. The man holding the reins is his cousin and his friend, who agreed to come to this war without picking up a single weapon. Back in the Udyoga days, Arjuna chose Krishna that way, unarmed. Now the choice pays off in a way no one planned. Session three of six: the moment a soldier becomes a student.
screen: `A CHARIOT BETWEEN TWO ARMIES` → `THE DRIVER CARRIES NO WEAPON` → `A SOLDIER BECOMES A STUDENT`

segments.voice: At the start of the Gita's second chapter, Krishna first tries a soldier's language. Shake off this weakness, he says. Stand up. It doesn't work. Arjuna answers with questions. How can he shoot arrows at Bhishma and Drona, men he should be honoring? Better to live as a beggar than to eat food stained with their blood. He doesn't even know which would be worse: winning or losing. Then he says the line that changes everything. I am your disciple. Teach me. I've come to you for refuge. He tells Krishna plainly that he will not fight, and falls silent. Notice where this happens. Not in a forest hermitage, not in a quiet room with a lamp, but in the open, between two armies, with a teacher who is also the driver. And the text gives a small detail here: Krishna, as if smiling, begins to speak. What he says first is startling to a man who has just refused to kill his family. You grieve for those you shouldn't grieve for. There was never a time when I was not, nor you, nor these kings, and there will never be a time when we cease to be. The body is worn and cast off, the way a person puts away old clothes. What's real in each of them cannot be killed. Read in place, this lands differently. It isn't a seminar on the soul. It's an answer to one terrified man, about particular people standing across the field: his grandfather, his teacher, his kin.
screen: `STAND UP: A SOLDIER'S WORDS FAIL` · `I AM YOUR DISCIPLE. TEACH ME.` · `KRISHNA, AS IF SMILING` · then, large: `WHAT'S REAL CANNOT BE KILLED`

segments.voice: Let your breath be the reins: steady, not tight. Bring to mind a question you haven't been able to answer on your own, and don't solve it; breathing in, let it be there, and breathing out, let yourself be its student for a while. If you pray, you can bring that question into your prayer.
Bhishma Parva. The book of the battle where, before a single arrow flies, a soldier asks to be taught.
Your line: I am your disciple, teach me. The great archer's first step is to ask. Day eight hundred twenty-one, done.

chat.meaning: Arjuna takes refuge as Krishna's disciple and asks to be taught. Then Krishna, as if smiling, begins the teaching between the two armies.
